messages:
priya: quick sync — AcmeHealth asked for two things: (1) "auto quantization recommendations" that are "quality-aware" (i.e., flag any regressions on eval sets) and (2) realtime eval-triggered alerts when their production outputs drift vs baseline. they want this in the Optimize toolkit pilot.

priya: high level ask from them is: reduce token cost via quant+batching but *never* silently degrade quality. they want alerts + a recommended quant profile per model/workload.

diego: sounds reasonable. main tradeoffs: (a) running evals often costs compute and can add latency to decision loops, (b) running automatic quant tests for each candidate profile multiplies inference permutations. we need a gating policy.

maya: proposal from ML side: maintain small, targeted eval sets per customer (10-50 examples) for fast checks. run two levels: quick sampling checks (cheap, fast) and nightly / pre-rollout full evals. only promote profiles that pass both.

ava: confirming customers will allow uploading private eval sets? AcmeHealth said yes (gov/regulatory data scrubbed). we'll need clear UX: "attach eval set" + "alert threshold" + opt-in for auto-promote.

sam: infra constraints: we can run quick sampling in the hosted Optimize pipeline (low-cost) but for per-customer full quant tests we should schedule on Dedicated pools or spot machines to avoid noisy-neighboring production. autoscale jobs but cap concurrency.

priya: MVP launch criteria idea (draft):
- Must-have: UI to upload/select eval sets and set drift thresholds.
- Must-have: automated quick-check that rejects quant profiles causing >X% drop on core metrics (configurable).
- Must-have: alerting to email/Slack + webhook when drift triggers.
- Should-have: suggested quant profiles (FP16/INT8 variants) with estimated token savings.
- Nice-to-have: auto-canary rollout (traffic split + rollback) for a promoted profile.

ava: customers will treat the suggested savings number as a commitment. include a disclaimer + per-workload estimate +/- variance. need the cost calc exposed in Console.

diego: internals: we should represent profiles as a tuple (model_variant, quant_level, kernel_hint). evaluation path: run deterministic eval -> compare metric vector -> compute delta. we need a compact snapshot that can be stored with model version to roll back.

maya: for metric comparison use paired bootstrap to get confidence intervals for small eval sets. alert only if delta exceeds threshold AND CI excludes zero. reduces false positives.

sam: landing & rollout plan:
- Phase 1 (pilot): manual triggers only, run quick-checks + alerts. target 3 pilot customers (including Acme).
- Phase 2: recommended profiles surfaced in Console; customers can accept.
- Phase 3: optional auto-promote with canary + rollback rules.

priya: what are the main blocking risks? list from eng: compute costs, false positives, and security/compliance for eval data. plus we need SLOs for the eval pipelines.

diego: to mitigate compute costs: do incremental quant tests — re-use cached KV / prefix comps and early-stop tests when metric drift obvious. also use simulated quant (weight perturbation) as a cheap prefilter.

maya: threat model: adversarial eval sets could cause unnecessary rollbacks/alerts. require eval sets to come from verified accounts and rate-limit eval-run requests. log provenance.

ava: acceptance criteria customers care about: (1) alert noise < 1 per month per model, (2) estimated cost savings within 20% of actual in first week, (3) no user-visible latency regressions outside configured SLO.

priya: can someone sketch the alert config UX? idea: 
```
alert: {
  eval_set: "acme-prod-samples",
  metric: "exact_match|emb_cos_sim",
  threshold: -0.03,  # negative means regress by 3%
  window: "last_30m",
  confidence: 0.95,
  notify: ["webhook:https://...","slack:#acme-ops","email:engops@acme.com"]
}
```
this should be editable per-customer.

sam: that looks good. implement as a rule object stored in Console. we'll add rate-limits and a "test rule" button that runs a dry-run and shows expected alerts.

diego: work breakdown rough estimate:
- Eval infra & quick-check pipeline: 3 wks
- Quant test harness + caching + early-stop: 4 wks
- Console UI + rule editor + telemetry: 3 wks
- Alerts/webhooks + notifications plumbing: 1.5 wks
- Pilot onboarding & runbooks: 1 wk
(total ~12 wks with parallel work)

priya: ok. can we reduce to an 8–9 week MVP by cutting auto-canary and full-nightly tests initially? focus on quick-checks + alerting + recommended profile list.

diego: yes, drop auto-canary and nightly full-eval from MVP. keep nightly only for internal audits at low frequency.

maya: agreement: MVP evaluates only small eval sets and uses CI-based gating. full-scale nightly runs are Phase 2.

ava: I'll draft the customer-facing pilot FAQ and required consents. will also collect 3 pilot customers this week.

ops-bot: action items created: PROD-OPT-212 (eval pipeline), PROD-OPT-213 (quant harness), PROD-OPT-214 (console rule editor), PROD-OPT-215 (pilot onboarding). Owners: diego, maya, sam, ava. Sync scheduled: Thu 11am.

priya: thanks — i'll assemble a one-pager for execs with the MVP scope and risk mitigations. follow-up Thurs.
